finding_mappings.finding: Welcomes beginners and experienced students; directs newcomers towards community participation and specialist interests.
Four main routes: News, Team, Events and Sponsors. The browser resolves Events to a separate platform; the text retriever misrepresented that URL.
Homepage combines membership FAQs and external academic/community resources. Team history and partner descriptions occupy dedicated pages.
The events platform exposes search, SIG filters, a calendar and sign-in. Controls were observed; filtering, authentication and event booking were not completed.

Desktop uses a dark canvas and pixel-style identity. The initial screen emphasises Discord; finding the next event requires navigation. Zero-valued counters in retrieved content should not be treated as real metrics.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Specialist groups, academic links and chat offer repeat value even when the public event queue is empty.
Team page explains weekly meetings and AGM elections, presents a year archive and links meeting minutes and a constitution. Linked documents were not individually audited.
Sponsors page groups organisations by tier and describes them. This establishes recognition; package deliverables and pricing were not observed in inspected material.
Strong combination of newcomer reassurance and institutional memory. The captured events queue is empty; that does not establish inactivity across the society.
High: coordinate events across SIGs and systems; medium for annual people/partner updates. Assign one calendar owner and preserve the committee archive.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: The homepage helps prospective members join and existing members find activities; partners receive a separate enquiry route.
Events, Photos, Projects, Contact and Calendar sit in the primary navigation, with About grouped separately. Footer repeats joining and committee routes.
The inspected event detail adds time zone, price, expected experience and workshop content. Calendar instructions and a navigable constitution support separate tasks.
Calendar page offers webcal, Google Calendar and a copyable feed address. Event detail exposes an add-to-calendar control. Subscription/import success was not tested.
Green mascot, generous spacing, large sans-serif headings and a prominent next-event card create a coherent desktop hierarchy. A skip link is exposed; overall accessibility remains unaudited.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Upcoming workshops, photos and a subscription route support attendance and return visits. Joining redirects to the Students’ Union for membership terms.
Named officers are public. The constitution explains elections, role responsibilities and finances with section anchors, making governance discoverable without relying on portraits alone.
Partners page provides recognition and committee contact, but no detailed public package comparison was observed.
Strong public event journey and explicit local time. Venue TBC remains a planning gap. Initial text retrieval failed on three details, but browser inspection recovered them.
Medium–high: events need weekly edits and confirmed venues; committee changes annually. A single feed can reduce duplication if used as the authoritative event source.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Serves computing students through community and industry opportunities; its services page also addresses organisers in other Imperial societies.
Primary Sponsors, About, Portal and Blog routes; Documents, Education, Software Foundation and Services are grouped under More.
About gives people, location and activities. Sponsorship explains reach and channels. Services enumerates equipment and supplies with an enquiry checklist.
Public routes lead to a member portal and IC Hack. Services use email to request equipment, dates and event details. Portal features and availability of equipment were not tested.
Blue header and compact white content area make the desktop presentation restrained. Sponsors appear early; a newcomer looking for a current routine event must follow another route.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Hackathon, industry activities and practical services offer several participation routes. The visible blog is weaker as a current return trigger.
Named officers include academic, event, communications, sponsor liaison and web responsibilities. Documents is linked, but its content was not inspected.
Explains sponsor access through events, emails and job advertisements; lists Gold, Silver and Bronze supporters. Its audience figure is self-reported, not independently verified.
Good example of a commercial proposition beyond a logo wall. Homepage’s latest visible post is April 2024, with several April-first posts; those are poor evidence of recent operations.
High if services are active: inventory, bookings and accountable owners are needed. Medium for partner and officer edits; blog freshness requires an explicit editorial commitment.
Welcomes different skill levels and offers technical learning, competitions and social participation. Joining is priced explicitly on the homepage.
Browser reveals About, Events, Follow Us, Mailing List and Become a Member. Nested routes include committee, constitution, sponsors and Learn to Code.
Dedicated beginner page explains who can attend, what to bring and when to arrive. Events appear through a calendar and a separate termcard image.
Google Calendar embed, external Stripe joining route, role email links and GitHub course materials are visible. Checkout and calendar subscription were not tested.

Dark blue background, monospaced display text and neon accents establish a computing identity. The termcard image needs an equivalent text listing for dependable access; no claim is made about its full alt text.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: A recurring course and reusable notes provide reasons to revisit. Multiple social channels carry updates when event plans change.
Committee page exposes specialist roles, selected role contacts and past office holders. Constitution is a visible route but was not read in this investigation.
Tiered recognition is substantial. Public package terms and a dedicated prospective-sponsor proposition were not observed in the inspected sponsor content.
Excellent practical first-session guidance. Separating an image termcard, calendar and social updates creates a potential reconciliation burden; actual synchronisation was not assessed.
Medium: refresh course details each term and people annually. Maintaining both a graphic termcard and calendar risks duplicate date edits; linked teaching materials also need review.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Combines student community, practical support and career opportunities with a clear offer for prospective partners.
Task-oriented navigation exposes About, Contact, Events, Jobs, Sponsor us, Tutorials and Wellbeing. Resource content is a first-class destination.
Tutorial catalogue supports study and practical skills. Wellbeing directory provides support routes. Sponsorship lists activities and information needed to start a conversation.
Tutorials include calendar-sync and site-contribution guidance. Sponsorship offers an email fallback when the contact form requires JavaScript; form delivery was not tested.
Desktop combines a photographic header with compact navigation and event cards. Short labels help scan tasks, although the top navigation is visually small in the capture.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Learning resources, jobs navigation and practical support add utility between events. Contributor guidance creates a route for members to improve the site.

Sponsor content explains ongoing committee dialogue and supplies role-based contact. About provides committee/course-rep email, constitution and Union society links; a named officer roster was not observed.

Describes year-long packages, talks, custom events and outreach; asks for organisation, budget and interest. Standard and Premium lists appear identical in retrieved text; differences need clarification.
Strong sponsor decision support. Homepage “Coming up” includes 26–27 October 2026 dates already past on investigation day. Sponsor copy cites a 2020 ranking, so reach/context claims need dating.

High editorial breadth: event expiry, jobs, tutorials and support contacts all need owners. Medium for annual sponsor review. Link to authoritative support services rather than duplicating changing advice.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Addresses students seeking technical, social and academic activities, including learners outside computer science.
Single-page sections cover membership, events, activities, team and supporters; committee history has its own page.
Activity descriptions explain workshops, competitions, industry talks, trips and support. Past Royal Hackaway editions provide continuity.
Membership is delegated to the Students’ Union; Discord, email and hackathon sites are linked. No membership completion or event registration was attempted.
Large black headings on white, red membership/email actions and a contrasting Discord action make the desktop introduction straightforward. Long single-page structure may need anchor navigation.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Flagship hackathon and community chat provide clear participation routes. Other activity descriptions are less useful for planning without a dated routine schedule.
Named officers and year-labelled past committees are public. The homepage still labels its team 2025–2026; whether it remains the valid committee is unverified.
Supporter section invites sponsorship, but its linked destination could not resolve in the browser. Package detail and named sponsors were not established.
Clear membership/chat choices and historical continuity. January 2026 hero promotion and older committee label deserve review; v10 is mentioned separately as forthcoming.
Low–medium for the brochure structure, rising around the annual hackathon. Refresh hero promotions, committee year and sponsor destination during handover.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Welcomes novice and experienced Durham students through programming, workshops, talks and hackathons.
Events, Sponsors, Team, DurHack and Contact make a small primary navigation. Footer links Students’ Union policies and public source code.
Team descriptions explain who manages finances, publicity, technical work and sponsorship. Partner profiles link onward to careers information.
Contact form includes society/event routing and reCAPTCHA. Submission and validation were not tested; the dedicated Events route failed text retrieval.
Desktop uses a photographic community hero with a white text panel and black navigation. The high-level action is joining; current event availability is less clear from the captured homepage.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Weekly activity promise and DurHack give participation hooks. Visible homepage ball promotion says 15 June without an exposed year, limiting freshness assessment.
Every inspected executive role has a concise responsibility summary. Previous-executive link offers continuity; the archive itself was not audited.
Named sponsor profiles and careers links benefit members; a sponsorship invitation is visible. Public tiers, deliverables and pricing were not observed.
Best compact example of explaining committee jobs. An undated-year event promotion makes it difficult to decide whether the homepage offers a future activity.
Medium: maintain current event details, officer responsibilities and recruitment links. Contact form adds integration upkeep beyond static email.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Aims to connect students through events, practical learning and collaborative projects. The public navigation gives participation several forms.
Home, Events, Bootcamps, Project Proposals, Committee, Projects and Login/Register structure the site. Homepage chat links resolve; some deep-page footer links were placeholders in captured states.
Bootcamps provide dates, facilitators, topics and prerequisite guidance. Committee timeline has year-labelled roles and usernames. Project records were not established.
A dynamic bootcamp list and committee timeline rendered in browser; an account entry is linked. Proposal submission, authentication and populated project overlays remain unverified.
finding_mappings.disposition: Conditional / do not infer a working workflow

finding_mappings.finding: Dark red/black desktop identity with a large logo; navigation is tucked into a menu even at captured desktop width. A horizontally explored committee history may be less discoverable than a plain list.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Bootcamps are concrete return value; a showcase and project recruitment could deepen participation if populated. Captured home state reports no events this week.
Timeline shows a current 2026–2027 marker and officer usernames. Human-readable names, detailed duties and governance documents were not established in inspected content.
No partner recognition or dedicated sponsor proposition was observed in the inspected pages. Project showcase potential is an analyst inference, not evidence of sponsor functionality.
Important retrieval lesson: the browser recovered bootcamp and committee content. Projects/proposals remained in loading states during capture, so they cannot be counted as populated features.
finding_mappings.disposition: Avoid indefinite loading; verify before adopting

finding_mappings.finding: High relative to a brochure: dynamic data, account routes, multiple content types and loading/error states need sustained ownership. Bootcamp archives also require careful past/future labelling.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Serves students through academic and social activity with School of Computer Science and industry relationships.
Small navigation separates Events, Committee, Sponsors, Contact and LeedsHack. Footer contains community and Students’ Union routes.
Events archive records venues and descriptions across technical, social and inclusive activities. Committee roles and sponsor careers information add practical context.
External LUU Engage route supports membership/tickets; event copy points to Discord or Engage where relevant. No checkout or registration was completed.
Dark blue desktop design and monospaced introduction establish a computing theme. The homepage’s animated title was partially rendered in capture; archives provide more concrete planning detail.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Event history demonstrates breadth, including non-alcoholic and targeted inclusion activities. Empty upcoming section gives existing visitors limited immediate planning value.
Named officers explain their responsibilities rather than listing titles alone. A past AGM entry describes questions and elections, though a governance document was not observed.
TPP and Jane Street profiles connect recognition to recruitment; a committee email invites sponsorship. Public packages or tiers were not observed.
Good event descriptions and responsibility clarity. No future events were listed at inspection; a recurring event described in an archive should not be assumed to remain scheduled.
Medium–high: maintain event archives without presenting recurrence as a current promise. Refresh people annually and partner recruitment text when opportunities change.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Welcomes students interested in programming and technology through hackathons, workshops and career development. The requested reference is a Students’ Union listing.
Global Union navigation surrounds society-specific Committee, Products, Key Information and Donate anchors. The listing links a separate society website.
Main listing presents officers and short constitutional aims. Membership is a separate product; a related Union event page supplies detailed attendance information.
Membership product is published as free for 2026/2027. The inspected event routes registration to MLH. Purchasing, account eligibility and registration completion were not tested.
Institutional red navigation and the society banner share the desktop page. Society-specific anchor buttons help within a long page, but global Union routes add competing choices.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Beginner reassurance and a concrete external event-registration route support participation. Membership supplies a clear ongoing affiliation route.
Committee is separated into signatories and non-signatories. Short constitution aims explain purpose; detailed elections and operating rules were not verified.
No dedicated commercial sponsorship offer or current partner list was observed in inspected society content. A donation section label does not establish a sponsor programme.

The event detail’s venue and accessibility labels are a useful attendance pattern. Main URL timed out in text retrieval but loaded in browser; search-cached sections differed from live browser content.
Low–medium when using Union membership/event infrastructure. Maintain consistency with any separate website; event access labels need confirmation for each venue.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Welcomes students across majors and experience levels, with separate topic communities under one computing organisation.
Committees, Initiatives, Events and About group a broad ecosystem. Footer supplies explicit team, internship, sponsor and portal routes.
Main site introduces committees; officers directory exposes organisational depth. Event page hands off to the portal and points to recorded past material.
Membership login, mailing list and calendar destination are visible. Portal calendar functionality was described by the public page, not authenticated or exercised.
finding_mappings.disposition: Prefer public tasks; defer a bespoke portal

finding_mappings.finding: Blue geometric hero and clear white layout create a coherent desktop identity. Broad dropdown categories and a very long officer directory may need careful wayfinding as the organisation grows.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Topic committees, recorded content, initiatives and mailing list offer multiple entry points. Events require another system, increasing the number of destinations to understand.
Directory groups leadership and officers, including development, operations and sponsorship roles. Names/classes are public; operational responsibilities and constitutional rules were not audited.
Sponsor page distinguishes direct sponsorship from departmental/venue support, explains homepage/marketing visibility and gives an email contact. Package tiers were not observed.
Strong ecosystem orientation and explicit partner attribution. A portal handoff can fragment first-visit event discovery; its actual login requirement for browsing remains unverified.
High: coordinate many committee destinations and a large people roster. Shared event data and documented ownership would reduce cross-site inconsistency; current backend was not audited.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: Serves students building, learning and socialising through interest groups; separates open participation from paid member benefits.

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: Browser navigation exposes About, Calendar, Store, Resources and Wiki. Group categories and search organise a much larger internal community.

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: Group cards provide topic summaries and contacts. Resources explains membership benefits and feedback; About clarifies leadership and corporate enquiries.

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: Browser showed dated event cards and RSVP links absent from text retrieval. Directory search and calendar controls are present; filtering, RSVP and calendar import were not completed.

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: Blue field, orange join action, community photo and white activity cards give the desktop page a clear hierarchy. Directory search supports scale; the long roster can overwhelm without filtering.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: Interest groups, regular activities and member resources support repeat visits. Resources explicitly says most group/social participation does not require payment.

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: About names central officers; home directory names group leaders. Infrastructure, academic, mentorship and corporate committees make distributed ownership visible.

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: Corporate enquiry emails are explicit. Resources describes a résumé book shared with sponsors; access, consent and security were not assessed. No public tier/package comparison was verified.

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: Strong relationship between community discovery and practical benefits. Text-only calendar showed September while browser home showed October/November items: rendering differences prevent a confident staleness claim.

finding_mappings.society_name: ACM at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
finding_mappings.finding: High: events, many group leaders, benefits and account-related services need distributed owners. Résumé and room-access workflows add operational work beyond editing pages.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.finding: Represents computing students across several degrees, addressing social, educational and professional needs. Published scale figures are self-reported.
About, Events, Resources, Sponsors and Contact form the browser navigation. About pins governance/FAQ routes; Resources groups links by the organisation responsible.
About describes mentoring and media. Resources links learning, enrolment guidance and student tools; attribution distinguishes CSESoc material from DevSoc projects.
Terminal-like input is visible but command behaviour was not tested. Resources links degree planning, room finding, timetabling and course reviews; those external tools were not audited.
finding_mappings.disposition: Curate external tools; do not claim to operate them

finding_mappings.finding: Dark terminal/editorial theme, code-like headings and repository-style About content provide a distinctive desktop identity. The large sparse hero delays concrete actions in the captured view.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Learning, media and student tools provide value between events. Full event listings are delegated to Facebook, so a visitor may need an external platform for current planning.
About links current/past constitutions and an election nomination guide. These are discoverable governance routes; the linked documents and a current officer roster were not verified.
Tiered partner logos give recognition, including Diamond/Gold/Silver groups. A public benefits comparison and dedicated sponsor enquiry were not observed in inspected sponsor content.
Useful ecosystem curation with explicit ownership attribution. Retrieved Events lists 2025 activities and points to Facebook; the website alone did not establish the current event programme.
High for a media/tool ecosystem; medium if the main site only curates maintained links. Guides need year review, partner tiers annual review, and events a clear authoritative source.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: A student computing community offering events and practical computing infrastructure; membership grants access to documented services.

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: About groups team, members, constitution and supporters; Resources groups services, usage, talks, wiki, advice and internships. Get Involved is a separate entry point.

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: Services explains access and support; Get Involved distinguishes first signup and renewal. Constitution provides detailed rules; supporters page names funded outcomes.

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: Public instructions document account/hosting services, payment routes and manual activation. Actual service availability, provisioning and payments were not tested.

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: Light desktop palette, mascot and clear headings make the landing page approachable. Long service/rule pages use internal contents links; a theme toggle is exposed but not audited.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: Computing services, technical resources and mailing lists create utility beyond events. Homepage reported no upcoming events at capture.

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: Constitution sets duties, elections, finances and membership rights. Get Involved explains organising teams and systems recruitment; public governance is unusually actionable.

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: Supporters are credited against specific equipment and projects. Services documents an opt-in industry mailing list. A standard commercial tier programme was not observed.

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: Strong task instructions and funding accountability. Membership requires follow-up after payment, creating a manual completion dependency that newcomers must understand.

finding_mappings.society_name: University of Waterloo Computer Science Club
finding_mappings.finding: High operations: infrastructure, account support, security and succession require a systems team. Medium editorial work for instructions; copying this service scope would exceed an ordinary website project.
Supplied supplementary reference, not a fifteenth independent society. Helps students discover projects and start contributing.
Small Projects, Contribute and GitHub navigation; homepage also routes to learning and ACM events.
Project directory gives descriptions, languages/topics and code links. Contribution page explains Git workflow and first-task discovery.
Search field, repository links and activity feed are visible. Good-first-issue section showed one project/issue at retrieval; search and pull-request submission were not tested.
Minimal white desktop layout and short action cards keep entry choices legible. Raw repository activity may be less meaningful to beginners than a short curated task list.
finding_mappings.disposition: Design interpretation; no peer accessibility certification

finding_mappings.finding: Concrete starter issues reduce the gap between interest and participation; recent activity offers a reason to return when data stays reliable.
Credits ACM at UCLA as maintainer and links back to the umbrella organisation. No independent governance or officer directory was observed.
No separate sponsor proposition observed; this reference demonstrates contribution design, not a sponsorship programme.
finding_mappings.disposition: Outside this reference’s remit; no sponsor inference

finding_mappings.finding: Strong beginner-to-task pathway. Directory includes projects beyond ACM management, so affiliation must not be confused with maintainer responsibility.
Medium–high: project metadata, API/feed failures, issue availability and review capacity need ownership. Start with a curated few projects before attempting a live ecosystem feed.
finding_mappings.disposition: Analyst estimate → owner and review rule
